1.reason: Bluish colour of deep sea water is due to scattering of blue light by water molecules.

2.reason: A rainbow is seen when the observer stands with the light source behind and faces the raindrops.

3.reason: At noon sunlight travels least atmosphere, so light is least scattered and reaches us as white.

4.reason: Twinkling of stars is due to atmospheric refraction through layers of varying refractive index.

6.reason: Least distance of distinct vision for a normal eye is 25 cm.

7.reason: At very high altitudes there is little/no atmosphere to scatter sunlight, so the sky appears dark.

8.reason: Presbyopia is caused by weakening of ciliary muscles and stiffening of the eye lens with age.

9.reason: Sky is blue because shorter wavelengths (blue/violet) are scattered more than longer wavelengths.

10.reason: The eye lens forms an image on the retina, the light-sensitive screen.

12.reason: The eye lens forms a real and inverted image on the retina. Options B and D are duplicate; choose B.

13.reason: REVIEW: Rainbow forms by refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection. Best fit involving dispersion + TIR is (3 and 4) = C; options C and D are identical, making the item flawed.

14.reason: Myopia is corrected by a concave lens of focal length = far point = 1.4 m; power P = -1/1.4 = -0.71 D (negative for concave).

15.reason: Red has the longest wavelength and is least scattered, so it penetrates fog/dust/smoke best.

16.reason: Red light is least scattered and travels farthest, so it is used for danger signals.

17.reason: Cataract is the clouding/opacity of the eye lens.

18.reason: Accommodation: the lens changes focal length (thickness) to focus on objects at different distances.

19.reason: Most refraction of incoming light occurs at the cornea (the eye's outermost refracting surface).

20.reason: Twinkling of stars is due to atmospheric refraction of starlight.

21.reason: Rainbow results from the combined effect of refraction, dispersion and (total internal) reflection.

22.reason: The human eye works by refraction of light through cornea and lens to form an image on the retina.

23.reason: Rods are sensitive to the intensity (brightness) of light; cones are sensitive to colour.

25.reason: Statements (i) and (ii) are correct. (iii) is wrong (advanced sunrise/delayed sunset are due to atmospheric refraction, not reflection). So only (i) and (ii) = C.

26.reason: A prism deviates the emergent ray; a rectangular slab only laterally shifts it (emergent ray parallel, no net deviation).

27.reason: REVIEW: Statement 2 (accommodation) is true but does not directly explain Statement 1's claim. Best fit: both true, S2 not the correct explanation = D. Options A and B are identical, making the item ambiguous.

28.reason: Seeing near objects but not distant ones is myopia (short-sightedness).

30.reason: Wavelength order: violet < yellow < red. So lambda_v < lambda_y < lambda_r = A.

31.reason: Choroid absorbs/prevents reflection (ii); Retina detects light stimulus (i); Cornea helps focus entering light (iv); Iris controls pupil size (iii). So (a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii) = C.

32.reason: Ciliary muscles change the curvature (focal length) of the eye lens during accommodation.

33.reason: Presbyopia with both defects needs bifocal lenses: upper part concave (distant vision), lower part convex (near vision).

34.reason: Can see far but not near = hypermetropia, corrected by a convex (converging) lens.

36.reason: At sunrise/sunset, blue is scattered away leaving red; scattering causes the reddish sun.

37.reason: Splitting of white light into component colours by a prism is dispersion.

38.reason: In a normal eye the image always forms on the retina, so the image distance remains unchanged (the eye accommodates).

39.reason: Rainbow forms by refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection within raindrops. Option C (internal reflection) best matches.

40.reason: Splitting of light into component colours is dispersion.

41.reason: Rainbow involves refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection in water droplets.

42.reason: The pupil is the aperture that allows light to enter the eye.

43.reason: REVIEW: Snellen vision 6/9 means the patient reads at 6 m the letters a normal eye reads at 9 m. Option B states this.

44.reason: REVIEW: Atmospheric refraction causes (1) advanced sunrise/delayed sunset and (2) stars appearing higher. Rainbow=dispersion/TIR, blue sky=scattering. So (1 and 2) = A. Printed option labels were garbled; reconstructed as standard.

46.reason: Red light is scattered the least, so it travels farthest and is seen from a distance.

47.reason: The visible spectrum (VIBGYOR) is a band of 7 colours.

48.reason: The Moon has no atmosphere, so no scattering occurs and the sky appears black.

49.reason: The iris controls the size of the pupil and thus the amount of light entering the eye.

50.reason: Fine dust particles scatter shorter wavelengths most, so blue light is mainly scattered.

51.reason: Violet has the shortest wavelength and is refracted (deviated) the most by a prism.

53.reason: From an aeroplane (high above), a rainbow can be seen as full concentric circles (both primary and secondary).

55.reason: Hypermetropia (far-sightedness) is corrected using a convex (converging) lens.

62.reason: REVIEW: Atmospheric refraction = twinkling of star (i); Scattering = red colour of rising sun (iii); Dispersion = rainbow (ii); Tyndall effect = white colour of clouds (iv). So (a-i,b-iii,c-ii,d-iv) = A. Only options A and B were visible in the source; C and D reconstructed as distractors.

63.reason: Prism = medium bounded by two plane refracting surfaces (i); Spectrum = splitting of white light (iii); Tyndall effect = scattering in colloidal solution (ii); Rainbow = spectrum from rain drops (iv). So (a-i,b-iii,c-ii,d-iv) = B.

64.reason: Statements (1) diameter ~2.3 cm and (2) iris controls pupil are correct. (3) is wrong (most refraction occurs at the cornea, not lens). (4) is wrong (focal length of lens is adjusted, not lens-retina distance). So (a) and (b) = C.

65.reason: In air (effectively vacuum), all colours of light travel at the same speed c.
